mainTopic: Who must own the material of a גט: the ציץ's writing, a גט on gold as כתובה payment, keeping the paper, and גיטין on a slave or a slate
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of the ציץ: its letters stood out like the design on a gold coin but were worked from the outside, so they count as 'writing'. רבא asks רב נחמן about a גט written on a gold plate that the husband also gives as the כתובה payment, and רב נחמן says both take effect. A ברייתא seems to say only the blank leftover can pay the כתובה, but רב נחמן explains that blank space is part of the גט's margin unless the husband says otherwise. A ברייתא then teaches that if the husband keeps the paper she is not divorced, but a condition to return it is fine. רב פפא's question about keeping only the spaces between lines or words stays unresolved (תיקו). רמי בר חמא asks about a גט on the hand of the husband's slave who is found with the wife. After a debate with רבא about forgery, resolved by saying the writing is a tattoo, ריש לקיש's rule about wandering animals shows that this proves nothing. רמי בר חמא then asks about the wife's slate found with the husband. אביי tries to prove from the old man who wrote his own loan documents that she transferred it to him, and רבא begins to reject the proof, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Pushed-out letters are not real writing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ציץ needs actual 'writing', and letters pressed out from behind do not seem to be writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we need 'a writing', as the פסוק says about the ציץ? And here there is no writing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the description given just before this, that the letters of the ציץ were pushed out from behind. It argues that this does not seem to count as writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the ציץ says the words were 'written'. If the letters were only pressed out from the back, nobody actually wrote or carved letters, so the requirement seems to be missing.

keyTerms.meaning: a writing (the word the פסוק uses about the ציץ)
the gold plate the כהן גדול wears on his forehead

phrases.english: But we need 'a writing', and there is none!
phrases.notes: The word 'writing' comes from the פסוק about the ציץ, שמות 39:30.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ציץ discussion from earlier on the daf by attacking the claim that the letters were pushed out from behind.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ציץ's letters were pressed out from behind
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires 'writing'. Pushing letters out from behind is not writing, so the ציץ would not meet the requirement.

steps.title: Like gold coins in one way, unlike them in another
steps.stepSummary: The letters stood out like the design on gold coins, but they were made from the outside, so they count as writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was like gold dinars, and not like gold dinars. It was like gold dinars in that the letters stand out. It was not like gold dinars because there, on the coin, the work is done from the inside, and here, on the ציץ, it is done from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ציץ was only partly like a stamped gold coin. The way its letters were made is different enough that they count as writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ and a coin share one feature: the letters stand out from the surface. They differ in how this is done. On a coin the design is pressed 'from the inside', while on the ציץ the letters were worked 'from the outside'. Because the letters themselves were directly worked on, they count as writing.

keyTerms.meaning: stands out / sticks out from the surface

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the letters lay flat. They still stand out like a coin's design. The only difference is how they were made, and that difference is what makes them count as writing.

phrases.english: Like gold dinars, and not like gold dinars.
Like gold dinars, in that it stands out;
and not like gold dinars,
because there it is from the inside;
phrases.notes: 'There' means the gold coins.

phrases.english: and here, it is from the outside.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the ציץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by explaining exactly how the ציץ's letters were made.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the case: it is only partly like a coin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Letters that stand out like a coin's design were stamped, not written.
steps.terutzMaskana: The letters were worked from the outside, so they count as writing even though they stand out.
steps.whatToRemember: The ציץ's letters stood out like a coin's design, but they were worked from the outside, and so they count as the 'writing' the פסוק requires.

steps.title: A גט on a gold plate that also pays the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן whether a גט written on gold can also serve as the כתובה payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: if a husband wrote a גט for his wife on a gold plate and told her, 'Receive your גט, and receive your כתובה', what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא asks whether one gold plate can do two jobs at once: be the גט and also be the payment of her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gold plate is worth money, so the husband wants it to count as both the divorce document and the money he owes her for the כתובה. The question is whether the object the גט is written on can also be handed over as payment.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked him (a question of law)
the money a husband owes his wife when the marriage ends

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: כָּתַב לָהּ גֵּט עַל טַס שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: If he wrote her a get on a plate of gold,
and said to her: 'Receive your get
and receive your ketubah', what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It connects to the earlier one only through the idea of writing on a gold plate.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the gold plate a גט is written on also count as the payment of the כתובה?

steps.title: Both the גט and the כתובה take effect
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that she has received both her גט and her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: her גט has been received, and her כתובה has been received.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rules that the gold plate works for both jobs at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן, using the gold as payment does not get in the way of it being a valid גט. The woman is divorced and her כתובה is paid with the same object.

phrases.english: He said to him: her get has been received
and her ketubah has been received.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נִתְקַבְּלָה גִּיטָּהּ וְנִתְקַבְּלָה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both take effect: the gold plate is a valid גט and also pays the כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written on gold can also serve as the כתובה payment.

steps.title: A ברייתא where only the leftover pays the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא in which the husband says that the remainder, the blank part, is for the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged him from a ברייתא: if the husband said, 'Receive your גט, and the rest is for your כתובה', then her גט has been received, and the rest goes to her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן's answer. Here the גמרא is only quoting the source; the next step explains why it causes a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the husband does not say the whole document pays the כתובה. Only the 'rest' does, meaning the part with nothing written on it. That careful wording becomes the basis of the challenge.

phrases.english: He challenged him: 'Receive your get,
and the rest is for your ketubah',
phrases.notes: 'The rest' means the blank part of the material, where the גט is not written.

phrases.english: her get has been received, and the rest is for her ketubah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to challenge רב נחמן's ruling in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the gold plate pays the כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assigns only the blank leftover to the כתובה. The next step draws out why that is a problem for רב נחמן.

steps.title: Without a leftover, the כתובה is not paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the ברייתא that the payment works only because there is a leftover. Without one, it would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it works is that there is a leftover part. But if there is no leftover part, it would not work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the challenge. The ברייתא works only because there is a blank leftover, which suggests that the part the גט is written on cannot also pay the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא carefully used only the blank part as payment. This suggests that the written גט itself cannot serve as payment. That seems to go against רב נחמן, who let the whole gold plate pay the כתובה. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: This is only an inference from the ברייתא. רב נחמן has not been proven wrong: in the next step he explains that the ברייתא does not require a leftover at all.

phrases.english: The reason is that there is a remainder,
but if there is no remainder, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאִיכָּא שְׁאָר, הָא לֵיכָּא שְׁאָר לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 5 and turns it against רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the blank leftover can pay the כתובה, then a gold plate with the גט written on it, and no leftover, should not pay the כתובה.

steps.title: The leftover is not required; the ברייתא teaches that he must say it
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that the ברייתא does not require a leftover. It teaches that even when there is one, it counts for the כתובה only if the husband says so.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same rule applies even when there is no leftover. The ברייתא is teaching that even when there is a leftover, it counts toward the כתובה only if he told her so. If he did not tell her, it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the inference from the last step. He says the ברייתא mentioned a leftover for a different reason, not because a leftover is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had inferred that the payment works only when there is blank space. רב נחמן turns this around: the ברייתא's real point is that the blank space needs a spoken statement. Without that statement it is not set aside for the כתובה, so his own ruling still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: the leftover (blank) part of the paper
this is what it comes to teach us

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying a leftover is needed. רב נחמן says the opposite: without any leftover the גט still counts as payment. The leftover case only teaches that he has to say it out loud.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא שְׁאָר;
phrases.english: The same is true even though there is no remainder;
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן answering רבא's challenge from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and this is what it teaches us:
that even though there is a remainder,
if he said it to her, yes;
phrases.notes: He means: if he told her the leftover is for her כתובה, it counts.

phrases.english: if not, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא שְׁאָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inference drawn in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets why the ברייתא mentions a leftover
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא suggests a leftover is required for the payment to work
steps.terutzMaskana: No leftover is needed. When there is one, he must say explicitly that it is for the כתובה

steps.title: Why must he say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the leftover counts only if he says so explicitly.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב נחמן's rule. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems odd that a leftover piece would need to be named. The גמרא wants to know why it is not automatically part of the payment.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the leftover needs an explicit statement to count for the כתובה

steps.title: Blank space is the margin of the scroll
steps.stepSummary: The leftover normally counts as the margin of the גט, so it belongs to the גט unless he sets it aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the margin of the scroll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: blank space around the writing is normally treated as part of the document, its margin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document normally has empty edges, and those edges are part of the document. So the leftover is assumed to be part of the גט, and it becomes a separate כתובה payment only if he says so.
steps.whatToRemember: A גט made of something valuable can count as the כתובה payment. But blank space is part of the גט by default, so it is set aside for the כתובה only if he says so out loud.

phrases.english: It is the margin of the scroll.
phrases.notes: Literally "the air of the scroll": the empty border that is part of any document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The leftover is treated as the margin of the גט unless he sets it aside

steps.title: Keeping the paper versus a condition to return it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if the husband says the paper stays his, she is not divorced. If he says she must return the paper, she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: "This is your גט, but the paper is mine." She is not divorced. "On condition that you return the paper to me." She is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a husband who tries to keep the paper of the גט. It is a new topic, also about who owns the material of the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife must own the גט itself. If the paper stays the husband's, she has not really received it. A condition to return it later is different: the גט is fully hers now, and returning it is just a promise she has to keep.
steps.confusionAlert: Both cases end with the husband getting the paper back, yet the results are opposite. The difference is ownership right now: in the first case he never gives her the paper. In the second case it is hers, and she only has to give it back later.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"This is your bill of divorce,
and the paper is mine": she is not divorced.
"On condition that you return the paper to me":
she is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ וְהַנְּיָיר שֶׁלִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ברייתא on the related theme of who owns the material of the גט
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping the paper means no divorce. A condition to return the paper still gives a valid divorce
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the rule that the wife must own the גט itself, which is the basis for רב פפא's question next.

steps.title: What about keeping the space between lines or words?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks: what if the husband keeps only the blank paper between the lines or between the words?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: between line and line, or between word and word, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a question that builds on the ברייתא: what if he keeps only the blank spaces inside the גט?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said keeping all the paper ruins the גט. Here the paper with the writing on it is hers, and he keeps only the gaps. The question is whether those inner gaps count as part of the גט she must own.

keyTerms.meaning: asks a question (often an unresolved one)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
Between line and line
and between word and word, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: בֵּין שִׁיטָה לְשִׁיטָה וּבֵין תֵּיבָה לְתֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא of step 10 to a partial case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether keeping only the blank spaces between lines or words makes the גט invalid

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא does not resolve רב פפא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer: תיקו, the question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether the inner gaps are part of the גט. So the case stays uncertain.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand (the question is left unresolved)

steps.whatToRemember: Keeping the paper of a גט means no divorce, but a condition to return it is fine. Whether keeping only the spaces between lines or words is a problem is left unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב פפא's question without a resolution
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא's question remains an open doubt

steps.title: Why not answer רב פפא from 'one ספר'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the decision to leave רב פפא's question open. The תורה says a גט is one ספר, so if the husband keeps the blank paper between the lines, the גט becomes several pieces and should be invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not answer it from the word 'ספר'? The תורה said one ספר, and not two or three ספרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 12, where רב פפא's question was left unresolved. It suggests a simple answer from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blank spaces between the lines stay the husband's, the written strips the wife gets are separate pieces. The תורה says 'ספר', meaning one single document, so several strips should not work. That would answer רב פפא's question right away, so why was it left open?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it from (a simpler source)
A document; the תורה's word for the גט
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: But let him derive it from 'a scroll': the Merciful One said one scroll,
phrases.notes: דברים 24:1

phrases.english: and not two or three scrolls!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the unresolved status of רב פפא's question
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to leave רב פפא's question unresolved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Keeping the spaces between lines splits the גט into several pieces, and the פסוק requires one ספר

steps.title: The question is about intertwined letters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב פפא was asking about a case where the letters are linked together, so the writing stays one connected piece even without the blank spaces.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed where the letters are intertwined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends leaving רב פפא's question open by narrowing it to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the letters are written so that they touch and connect, removing the blank space does not split the writing into separate pieces. So the 'one ספר' rule does not settle it, and the question stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a specific case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed where it is intertwined.
phrases.notes: He means the letters are joined, so the writing still holds together as one piece.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gaps would split the גט into several ספרים
steps.terutzMaskana: With intertwined letters the writing stays one unit, so the question remains open

steps.title: רמי בר חמא asks about a גט on a slave's hand
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks: the slave was known to belong to the husband, the גט was written on the slave's hand, and now the slave is found with the wife. Is she divorced?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: if they had a presumption that a slave belonged to him, and the גט was written on the slave's hand, and now the slave is found in her possession, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It is based on the משנה's case of writing a גט on a slave's hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the husband writes the גט on his slave's hand and gives her the slave. Here we only see the slave with her, and we don't know how he got there.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a question with no obvious answer)

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
If they had a presumption about a slave that he is his,
phrases.notes: 'His' means the husband's.

phrases.english: and the bill of divorce is written on his hand,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי הוּא יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדָהּ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and now he comes out from under her hand, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about a גט written on a slave
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the wife is divorced when the slave carrying the גט is simply found in her possession

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the doubt: did the husband give her the slave, or did the slave go to her on his own?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say he transferred the slave to her, or perhaps the slave entered her possession on his own?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two possibilities behind רמי בר חמא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband gave her the slave, she received the גט properly and is divorced. If the slave just went over to her, the husband never gave her the גט, and she is not divorced.

phrases.english: Do we say he transferred him to her,
or perhaps he entered on his own?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the doubt in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether being found with her shows the husband gave her the slave

steps.title: רבא: writing on skin can be forged
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the question should not even arise. Writing on a person's body can easily be forged, so such a גט would be invalid anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: But let him derive it from the fact that this is writing that can be forged!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the whole question. He says the גט fails for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must be written in a way that cannot easily be changed. Writing on skin can be rubbed off and rewritten, so the question of how the slave got to her does not matter.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דִּכְתָב שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהִזְדַּיֵּיף הוּא!
phrases.english: But let him derive it from the fact that it is writing that can be forged!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the premise of רמי בר חמא's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט on skin can be forged, so it is invalid regardless of how the slave reached her

steps.title: The משנה allows a גט on a slave's hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the משנה explicitly says a גט may be written on a slave's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבא, the משנה is difficult, since it says a גט may be written 'on the hand of a slave'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the challenge back on רבא, using the משנה. The next step answers this challenge for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If writing on skin were invalid because it can be forged, the משנה could not permit a גט on a slave's hand. Yet it does, so רבא's objection seems to go against the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a challenge to רבא, not to רמי בר חמא. The משנה supports writing on a slave's hand, which makes רבא's objection the difficult one.

phrases.english: But according to Rava, the mishna is difficult:
"on the hand of a slave"!
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which lists a slave's hand as a valid place to write a גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's objection in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that writing on skin is invalid because it can be forged
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly permits a גט written on a slave's hand

steps.title: The משנה fits רבא, but רמי בר חמא's question is still in trouble
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה according to רבא: witnesses saw the handing over, following רבי אלעזר. But that leaves רבא's forgery objection against רמי בר חמא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's true that the משנה is no problem for רבא: it speaks of witnesses who saw the handing over, and it follows רבי אלעזר. But for רמי בר חמא there is still a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא against the challenge from the משנה. It then turns around and says רמי בר חמא's question is still stuck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא can say the משנה is talking about a case where witnesses watched the slave being handed to the wife. According to רבי אלעזר, the witnesses to the handing over are what make a גט work, so forgery is no worry. In רמי בר חמא's case nobody saw the handing over, so רבא's worry that writing on skin can be faked still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable / granted (used to set up a contrast)
Witnesses who watch the גט being handed over

steps.confusionAlert: The 'problem for רמי בר חמא' is not a problem from the משנה. It is רבא's forgery objection, which still hits רמי בר חמא's question because no one saw the handing over in his case.

phrases.english: Granted, the Mishnah is not difficult for Rava,
it speaks of witnesses to the handing over, and it follows Rabbi Elazar.
But for Rami bar Chama it is difficult!
phrases.notes: He means רבא's forgery objection from step 17 still knocks out רמי בר חמא's question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 18 for רבא, then turns the difficulty back on רמי בר חמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רמי בר חמא's case no witnesses saw the handing over. Writing on skin can be forged, so the גט should be invalid no matter how the slave reached her, and the question never gets started.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא meant a tattooed גט
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא was asking about a גט tattooed onto the slave, which cannot be forged.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רמי בר חמא there is also no problem: he was asking about writing done as a tattoo.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rescues רמי בר חמא's question. It explains that he was talking about a tattoo, not ink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ink on skin can be rubbed off and rewritten, which is רבא's worry. A tattoo is permanent and cannot be changed, so forgery is not a concern. That means רמי בר חמא's real doubt, how the slave got to the wife, is a fair question.

keyTerms.meaning: Writing made as a tattoo (permanent marking in the skin)

phrases.aramaic: לְרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא –
phrases.english: For Rami bar Chama it is also not difficult –
it was written as a tattoo.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty against רמי בר חמא raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the question was about a tattoo.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the writing was in ink, which can be forged, so the question made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The writing is a tattoo, which cannot be forged, so the only doubt is how the slave came to the wife.

steps.title: The tattoo answer also explains the משנה for רבא
steps.stepSummary: Once we use the tattoo idea, the משנה can also be read as talking about a tattoo. So it no longer challenges רבא at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this idea, the משנה is also no problem for רבא: it too is talking about writing done as a tattoo.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the tattoo answer it just used and applies it to the משנה as well. That gives רבא a simpler defense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבא needed to say the משנה had witnesses to the handing over and followed רבי אלעזר. Now we can just say the משנה allows writing on a slave's hand because it is a tattoo, which cannot be forged. רבא's rule against ink writing on skin stays fully in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this (idea)

steps.whatToRemember: A tattooed גט on a slave cannot be forged. That one idea makes the משנה fit רבא and also keeps רמי בר חמא's question alive.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,
the Mishnah (for Rava) will also not be difficult –
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, but either way the point is that the משנה is no problem for רבא.

phrases.english: it is speaking of writing done as a tattoo.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the tattoo answer from step 20 and applies it to the משנה, giving רבא a new answer to step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about a tattoo.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה needed witnesses to the handing over and רבי אלעזר to fit רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a tattoo, which cannot be forged, so it never clashes with רבא's rule.

steps.title: So what is the answer to רמי בר חמא's question?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the question stands, the גמרא asks what the final ruling is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was decided about it?
steps.whatsHappening: With רמי בר חמא's question now valid, the גמרא asks for its final answer. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19 through 21 only showed that the question is a real one. The actual doubt is still open: the tattooed slave is found with the wife, so is she divorced? The גמרא now looks for a resolution.

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רמי בר חמא's original doubt now that it has survived רבא's objection.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the wife divorced when the tattooed slave known to be the husband's is found with her?

steps.title: ריש לקיש: wandering animals give no presumption of ownership
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings ריש לקיש's rule that straying animals carry no ownership presumption. So a slave who walks around on his own proves nothing, and she is not divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for ריש לקיש said: animals that wander have no presumption of ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a rule from ריש לקיש. Animals that roam around do not prove who owns them just because they are found in someone's place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually holding an object is a sign you own it. Animals that wander may simply have walked over by themselves, so having them proves nothing. A slave can walk too, so finding him with the wife does not show the husband gave him to her, and the גט was never shown to be handed over.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that wander or stray from place to place
A presumption, here a presumption of ownership

steps.whatToRemember: Something that moves around on its own does not prove ownership by being found with someone. So the wife is not divorced in רמי בר חמא's slave case.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Reish Lakish said:
Animals that wander have no presumption of ownership.
phrases.notes: The גמרא applies this to the slave: he can walk to her on his own, so being with her proves nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wandering animals, and likewise a slave who can walk, give no ownership presumption. We cannot assume the husband handed the slave over, so she is not divorced.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general principle: holding something proves ownership only when the thing could not have gotten there by itself.

steps.title: A new question: the wife's slate shows up in the husband's possession
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks about a slate known to be the wife's, with a גט written on it, that is now in the husband's hands. Did she really give it to him, or does a woman not understand how to give it over?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: everyone knew a slate was hers, and a גט was written on it, and now it comes out of his possession. What is the law? Do we say she gave him ownership of it, or perhaps a woman does not know how to transfer ownership?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא opens a new question. A slate known to belong to the wife has a גט on it, and now the husband has it and wants to divorce her with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must belong to the husband when he gives it. Since the slate was hers, it only works if she truly transferred it to him. Maybe she did, or maybe she did not take it seriously as a real transfer, since it was going right back to her, so it never became his.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raises a question that may stay unsolved)

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
If it was known that a slate was hers –
and a get was written on it;

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי הִיא יוֹצְאָה מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and now it comes out of his possession, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The husband now holds it and wants to divorce her by giving her this slate.

phrases.english: Do we say she transferred its ownership to him,
or perhaps (a woman) does not know how to transfer ownership?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about a slate known to be the wife's, after the slave question is settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a slate known to be the wife's, now in the husband's hands, count as his so that a גט on it works? Or do we assume a woman does not really transfer such an object?

steps.title: אביי cites the case of the old man who lent to his village
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a משנה about an old man near ירושלים who lent money to everyone in his village. He wrote the loan documents in his own handwriting, others signed them, and the חכמים ruled them valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear. He also testified about a small village next to ירושלים. There was one old man there who lent money to everyone in the village. He would write the documents in his own handwriting, and others would sign. The case came before the חכמים, and they ruled the documents valid.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a proof to answer רמי בר חמא's slate question by quoting a case from a משנה. Here he only lays out the case. The next steps explain why it proves anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is that the lender himself wrote the loan documents, so they were in his hands from start to finish. The חכמים still accepted them. אביי will use this to show that a quiet transfer of ownership can happen even when the item ends up back with the person who started with it.

keyTerms.meaning: He testified, meaning he reported a ruling or a past case

phrases.english: Abaye said: Come and hear:
He also testified
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יהודה בן בבא, who is quoted earlier in this משנה in עדיות.

phrases.aramaic: עַל כְּפָר קָטָן שֶׁהָיָה בְּצַד יְרוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: about a small village that was next to Jerusalem,
and there was one old man in it,
and he would lend money to all the people of the village,
and he would write the documents in his own handwriting
and others would sign,
and the case came before the Sages
and they ruled it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to answer רמי בר חמא's slate question from step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That we assume the wife gave ownership of the slate to the husband, so his giving it back to her works as a גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עדיות about the old man whose self-written loan documents were ruled valid by the חכמים.

steps.title: Why were the old man's documents valid?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks why the documents were valid. A document has to be handed over as a "ספר מקנה", but here it never left the lender's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why were they valid? We need a "deed of purchase", and here there isn't one!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a pointed question about the case he just quoted. This question sets up the point he is about to prove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "ספר מקנה" teaches that a document has to pass from the one obligating himself to the one receiving it. The old man wrote the document on his own paper and kept it, so it looks like nothing was ever handed over. That makes the חכמים' ruling seem puzzling.

keyTerms.meaning: "Deed of purchase" (ירמיהו 32:11): the document must be handed over from one side to the other
And it isn't there; it is missing

phrases.english: And why were they valid?
Don't we need a "deed of purchase",
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 32:11

phrases.english: and there isn't one here!
phrases.notes: The document stayed with the lender the whole time, so nobody seems to have handed it over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out a problem in the case from step 25 so that the solution can serve as the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' ruling that the old man's self-written documents are valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A valid document has to be handed over ("ספר מקנה"), but these documents were the lender's own paper and never left his possession.

steps.title: He must have given the paper to the borrowers first
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the old man must have transferred ownership of the documents to the borrowers, who then gave them back. In the same way, the woman can transfer the slate to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it because we say that he transferred ownership of the documents to them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his proof. The documents were valid because we assume the old man first gave the paper to the borrowers, so it really was handed from them to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case shows that we assume a transfer of ownership happened even though the item ends up back with the person who started with it. אביי applies this to the slate. We can assume the wife gave the slate to her husband, so when he hands it back to her it counts as a real גט.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather, isn't it...": introduces the only explanation that seems to work

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's proof: a person can give ownership of an item to someone else even when it will come right back to him. So the wife could have given her slate to her husband.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it because we say
that he transferred ownership of the documents to them!
phrases.notes: "Them" means the borrowers. They owned the paper, then handed the finished document back to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן אַקְנוֹיֵי מַקְנֵה לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the problem from step 26, and the solution becomes the proof for step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That the wife can transfer the slate to her husband, and he can then give it back to her as a גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The old man's documents were valid only because we assume he transferred the paper to the borrowers.

steps.title: רבא begins to reject the proof
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the difficulty is and starts to explain the old man's case another way with "perhaps".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And what is the difficulty? Perhaps...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens his rejection of אביי's proof. He says the question is not a real problem and starts offering another explanation, which continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By asking "what is the difficulty?", רבא means that the old man's case can be explained without assuming any transfer of ownership. If that is so, the case does not prove anything about the woman and her slate. His actual explanation comes after the word "perhaps".

keyTerms.meaning: "And what is the difficulty?": the question is not really a problem
Perhaps; introduces another way to explain the case

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends at "perhaps". רבא's actual explanation has not been given yet, so do not fill it in from guesswork.

phrases.english: Rava said: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to push back on אביי's proof from steps 25 through 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's proof from the old man's documents.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא says the question about "ספר מקנה" is no real difficulty and starts to offer another explanation (completed in the next section).
